summary: Owned units s0244–s0266 give no birth or death years for p084–p088. The only numeric age is 年數歲 for Wang Xianzhi (p082) at the chupu scene, which is an age-at-event and not a birth year. Huan Xuan’s 太尉 court assembly (s0245–s0247) is Huan Xuan’s and Wang Zhenzhi’s own event: Jin Andi 元興元年三月 he 自稱太尉, and Eastern Jin 元興元年 (ruler 晉安帝, not the Han or Wu 元興 eras) converts as AD 402; month 3 begins 18 April 402, so the 壬申 appointment stays AD 402 in Julian and proleptic Gregorian. That supports claim-645/684/685/712 and the p084–p085 hints. The visit 嘗與兄徽之、操之俱詣謝安 has no source year; AD 360–396 is an invented career/Taiyuan-end window, and 396 postdates Xie An’s death in 太元十年 (AD 385). 遠慚荀奉倩 / 近愧劉真長 are Xianzhi’s childhood comparisons, not Xun Can’s or Liu Tan’s own events; AD 240–249 and 330–347 treat later reception as living activity (240–249 also mismatches 荀粲傳 太和初, death at 29). No birth/death was omitted from these units because the Chinese does not state them.

itemChecks.event: Huan Xuan assumed the office of Grand Commandant and held a full court assembly.
itemChecks.reason: The dated office belongs to Huan Xuan (p085), not Zhenzhi or the late uncle. s0245 桓玄為太尉 names his own appointment. Jin Shu 安帝紀 records 元興元年三月 玄俄又自稱太尉 under 東晉 晉安帝 (distinct from Han Huandi and Wu 元興). 元興元年 is AD 402; the third month begins 18 April 402, so the 壬申 self-appointment remains AD 402 in Julian and proleptic Gregorian. 元興二年二月 he 自稱大將軍, so a tenure-only reading could reach early 403, but 朝臣畢集 is the Taiwei assembly of that appointment year, not a dynasty-long window. Year 402 is therefore the justified endpoint for this office-taking.

evidence.quote: 桓玄為太尉

itemChecks.event: Wang Xianzhi, then several years old, watched disciples play chupu.
itemChecks.reason: The age belongs to Wang Xianzhi (p082) at this childhood scene, not to a birth year and not to p084–p088. s0254 年數歲 is an explicit traditional inclusive age-at-event. The claim correctly keeps the Chinese statement and does not convert it into a Western birth year.

evidence.quote: 年數歲，嘗觀門生樗蒱

itemChecks.event: Wang Xianzhi once visited Xie An with his brothers Huizhi and Caozhi.
itemChecks.reason: The visit is Xianzhi’s own undated anecdote (owner p082). s0258 only has 嘗與兄徽之、操之俱詣謝安: 嘗 is an unspecified occasion, not a reign year. AD 360 and AD 396 are invented endpoints (office-taking guess plus 太元 era-end), not conversions of a source date. A window must state uncertainty about this one visit, not activity through an era. Jin Shu 孝武帝紀 places Xie An’s death in 太元十年八月, which converts as AD 385, so 396 cannot close the visit. The interval is unsupported and historically too late at the far end.

evidence.quote: 嘗與兄徽之、操之俱詣謝安

itemChecks.event: Wang Zhenzhi answered Huan Xuan at the Grand Commandant court assembly.
itemChecks.reason: The dated event is Zhenzhi’s own reply (p084), not a life date for the 亡叔. s0245 ties the question to 桓玄為太尉; s0247 is Zhenzhi’s answer. The same 元興元年三月 appointment converts as AD 402 (晉安帝 元興, month 3 after New Year). 402 dates this court exchange, not Zhenzhi’s undated 侍中 / 大司馬長史 career in s0244.

evidence.quote: 桓玄為太尉，朝臣畢集，問楨之
楨之曰：「亡叔一時之標，公是千載之英。」

itemChecks.event: Huan Xuan, as Grand Commandant, assembled the court officials.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Huan Xuan (p085). The attestation is the same Taiwei assembly as claim-645, justified by s0245 and the 安帝紀 元興元年三月 self-appointment, converted as AD 402. It is not Zhenzhi’s office and not the uncle’s lifetime. The single year is the appointment-assembly year, not a multi-reign activity span.

evidence.quote: 桓玄為太尉，朝臣畢集

itemChecks.event: Wang Caozhi visited Xie An together with Huizhi and Xianzhi.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Caozhi (p086), who is named in the visit, but the Chinese gives no year. AD 360–396 is not converted from 嘗與兄徽之、操之俱詣謝安 and is not his undated 侍中、尚書、豫章太守 list in s0250. The end year 396 is the last 太元 year and falls after Xie An’s 太元十年 (AD 385) death, so it cannot bound Caozhi’s visit. The source date remains unresolved.

evidence.quote: 嘗與兄徽之、操之俱詣謝安

itemChecks.event: The dated row does not record Xun Can’s own event; Wang Xianzhi recalled him as a distant exemplar.
itemChecks.reason: s0256 遠慚荀奉倩 is Xianzhi’s childhood comparison, a later reception of Xun Can (p087), not Xun Can’s own Cao Wei activity. Historical dating must date the named person’s own event; reception stays retrospective and must not supply life years or active hints. AD 240–249 is absent from this chapter (certainty “explicit” is false) and matches 曹魏 正始, not 何劭《荀粲傳》太和初 activity and death at twenty-nine. The Western interval is invented.

evidence.quote: 遠慚荀奉倩

itemChecks.event: The dated row does not record Liu Tan’s own event; Wang Xianzhi recalled him as a near exemplar.
itemChecks.reason: s0256 近愧劉真長 is the same Xianzhi remark, a near-exemplar reception of Liu Tan (p088), not Liu Tan’s own Eastern Jin office-holding. AD 330–347 is not in the Chinese and is not an explicit source date. Using that invented window as attestation dates later quotation as living activity. The mention must remain retrospective; this chapter does not justify either endpoint.

evidence.quote: 近愧劉真長

itemChecks.event: Xie An received the three Wang brothers and judged the youngest superior.
itemChecks.reason: Hosting and the ranking remark are Xie An’s own events (p089) in s0258–s0259, but they are undated (嘗; 既出，客問安). AD 360–396 does not convert a source year. 396 is 太元 twenty-first year, after 孝武帝紀 太元十年八月 謝安薨 (AD 385). The closed interval invents a second endpoint and treats an era span as the date of one visit.

evidence.quote: 嘗與兄徽之、操之俱詣謝安
客問安王氏兄弟優劣，安曰：「小者佳。」

itemChecks.event: Huan Xuan asked Zhenzhi how he compared with Zhenzhi’s late uncle.
itemChecks.reason: The court question is Huan Xuan’s own act (p085), dated from 桓玄為太尉 in s0245. 亡叔 marks the uncle already dead and must not feed the uncle’s life dates; it does not move this event off Huan Xuan. The 元興元年三月 Taiwei appointment converts as AD 402, the year of this question.

evidence.quote: 桓玄為太尉，朝臣畢集，問楨之：「我何如君亡叔？」

itemChecks.event: Wang Zhenzhi answered Huan Xuan’s comparison question when Huan Xuan was Grand Commandant.
itemChecks.reason: The hint restates Zhenzhi’s own 402 court reply, which is a supported personal event (claim-684), not posthumous reception and not his undated 歷位 offices. AD 402 is the Taiwei-assembly year justified above.

evidence.quote: 桓玄為太尉，朝臣畢集，問楨之
楨之曰：「亡叔一時之標，公是千載之英。」

itemChecks.event: Huan Xuan held the Grand Commandant office and questioned Zhenzhi before the assembled court.
itemChecks.reason: The hint matches Huan Xuan’s own Taiwei appointment and question, the supported AD 402 event in s0245. It is not an era-long activity hint and does not borrow the uncle’s death.

evidence.quote: 桓玄為太尉，朝臣畢集，問楨之

itemChecks.event: Wang Caozhi visited Xie An with his brothers Huizhi and Xianzhi.
itemChecks.reason: The visit is Caozhi’s own event, but the hint’s AD 360–396 range is not a source date and conflicts with Xie An’s death in 太元十年 (AD 385). Active hints may follow only supported personal chronology; this interval cannot stand.

evidence.quote: 嘗與兄徽之、操之俱詣謝安

itemChecks.event: The hint lacks Xun Can’s own dated event; it only records Wang Xianzhi later recalling him as a distant exemplar.
itemChecks.reason: The hint itself calls him a recalled distant exemplar, which is reception, then still assigns AD 240–249 as an active-date hint. Later quotation must not feed life dates or activity. This chapter has no Xun Can event to date.

evidence.quote: 遠慚荀奉倩

itemChecks.event: The hint lacks Liu Tan’s own dated event; it only records Wang Xianzhi later recalling him as a near exemplar.
itemChecks.reason: 近愧劉真長 is Xianzhi’s comparison, not Liu Tan acting. AD 330–347 is an invented Eastern Jin window used as an active hint. Reception dates cannot serve as life or activity hints.

evidence.quote: 近愧劉真長

personChecks.reason: Wang Zhenzhi’s only dated personal event in the supplied items is his Taiwei-court reply in AD 402 (claim-684; hints-p084). Owner of that date is Zhenzhi answering Huan Xuan, justified by 桓玄為太尉 and the 元興元年三月 appointment. s0244 歷位侍中、大司馬長史 has no year and needs none invented. Owned units give no birth, death, or age for him; 亡叔 is the uncle’s already-dead status, not Zhenzhi’s death, and does not disturb the 402 exchange.

evidence.quote: 楨之字公幹，歷位侍中、大司馬長史。
桓玄為太尉，朝臣畢集，問楨之
楨之曰：「亡叔一時之標，公是千載之英。」

personChecks.reason: Huan Xuan’s supplied items (office, attestation, court question, hint) all date his own Taiwei assembly in AD 402. Endpoints rest on s0245 plus the 安帝紀 元興元年三月 self-appointment, not on later 大將軍 / usurpation years. This passage is not his biography and states no birth or death; none is omitted from a blank source. The 402 event is not fed by anyone else’s posthumous reception.

evidence.quote: 桓玄為太尉，朝臣畢集，問楨之：「我何如君亡叔？」

personChecks.reason: Caozhi’s only dated item is the Xie An visit (claim-686; hints-p086) placed at AD 360–396. That interval is not in s0258 and cannot be his chronology: 396 is after Xie An’s 太元十年 death. s0250 lists offices without a year. Context items are empty; chapter-internal undated offices do not rescue the invented visit window. Person-level activity through 360–396 is unsupported.

evidence.quote: 操之字子重，曆侍中、尚書、豫章太守。
嘗與兄徽之、操之俱詣謝安

personChecks.reason: Xun Can appears only in Xianzhi’s 遠慚荀奉倩. That is retrospective reception, not a Cao Wei life event in this chapter. claim-687 and hints-p087 still assign AD 240–249 as attestation/activity. Those years are not in the Chinese, are the wrong era relative to 荀粲傳 太和初 and death at twenty-nine, and cannot be person chronology. No birth, death, or age is stated here, and none should be inferred from the comparison.

evidence.quote: 獻之怒曰：「遠慚荀奉倩，近愧劉真長。」

personChecks.reason: Liu Tan likewise appears only as 近愧劉真長, a near-exemplar recollection by Xianzhi. claim-688 and hints-p088 turn AD 330–347 into his attestation/activity. Those endpoints are not in this chapter and are not his own event. A later-written childhood scene cannot be used as Liu Tan’s life dates. Person chronology from this passage is reception-only and currently misdated.

evidence.quote: 近愧劉真長

findings.problem: The Xie An visit is undated (嘗). AD 360–396 is an invented era/career window, and 396 is after Xie An’s death in 太元十年 (AD 385). It describes activity through a period, not uncertainty about one visit.
findings.action: Drop both invented endpoints. Keep the visit as the brothers’ and Xie An’s own event with unresolved:true and a reason that 嘗 names no year; if a bound is added, use only a one-sided onOrBefore from the 太元十年 death (AD 385), not a new start year. Clear the 360–396 active hint for p086.

findings.problem: 遠慚荀奉倩 is Xianzhi’s later comparison, not Xun Can’s own event. AD 240–249 treats reception as living activity, is not in the chapter, and conflicts with 荀粲傳 太和初 / death at 29.
findings.action: Reclassify as retrospective-reference or receptionType retrospective on the childhood remark; remove the 240–249 attestation interval and the matching active-date hint. Do not invent a birth or death year from this mention.

findings.problem: 近愧劉真長 is the same Xianzhi recollection, not Liu Tan’s own event. AD 330–347 is an invented Eastern Jin activity window used as attestation and as an active hint.
findings.action: Reclassify as retrospective reception of Xianzhi’s remark; remove 330–347 from the attestation and from p088 active-date hints. Do not convert the comparison into Liu Tan life dates.
